evidence.claim: Williams disclosed Q1 2026 data-center-related projects including Atlas, an agreement to provide up to 164 MMcf/d of pipeline capacity for a large Northeast data-center customer by year-end 2026, and NEO, a 682 MW behind-the-meter power project targeted for service in the second half of 2028.
evidence.source_title: Q1 Earnings Recap: Data centers accelerate new growth paths for Williams

evidence.claim: Williams stated at its 2026 Analyst Day that LNG exports and power generation are primary long-term demand drivers and that data centers are expected to account for a large share of U.S. gas-fired electricity demand growth through 2035.
evidence.source_title: Natural gas infrastructure is the fix for surging energy demand

evidence.claim: Energy Transfer's January 2026 investor presentation stated that most 2026 growth capex would enhance its natural-gas pipeline network, and listed more than 105,000 miles of gas gathering/interstate/intrastate pipelines, more than 55 Bcf/d of pipeline throughput capacity, and about 236 Bcf of natural-gas storage capacity.

Energy Transfer's Q1 2026 materials disclosed demand-pull contracts from end users, data centers, and utilities totaling more than 6 Bcf/d of contracted pipeline capacity, with an 18-year weighted average life and more than $25 billion of expected firm-transportation-fee revenue.

Energy Transfer's Q1 2026 call discussed new pipelines and meter stations to provide natural gas to power plants and data-center sites in Oklahoma and Arkansas, and firm gas transportation for the Nexus Hubbard behind-the-meter AI hyperscale campus in Central Texas.
evidence.source_title: Energy Transfer Q1 2026 Earnings Call: Complete Transcript

evidence.claim: Kinder Morgan's 2Q 2026 investor presentation framed the company as positioned to meet surging data-center power demand and used 1 GW equals 0.15 Bcf/d of natural gas as a conversion assumption for potential data-center gas capacity needs.

RBN Energy summarized Kinder Morgan Q1 2026 commentary as emphasizing that U.S. gas infrastructure buildout is no longer only an LNG story, with rising gas-fired power demand tied partly to data centers and the Creekside Lateral targeted for 4Q 2026 to serve power, industrial, and data-center demand.

Cheniere's 2025 earnings materials pointed to a high-growth period for global LNG supply and demand from 2026 to 2030, supporting the company's linkage to global LNG demand rather than a narrow U.S. data-center power node.
First Solar reported Q1 2026 net sales of $1.04 billion, up 24% year over year, and contracted sales backlog of 47.9 GW as of March 31, 2026.
evidence.source_title: First Solar Q1 2026 Results Press Release

evidence.claim: First Solar's Q1 2026 earnings presentation listed a 47.9 GW and $14.4 billion contracted backlog.
Enphase reported Q1 2026 revenue of $282.9 million versus $343.3 million in Q4 2025; U.S. revenue declined about 23% sequentially due to Section 25D tax-credit expiration and seasonality.
evidence.source_title: Enphase Energy Reports Financial Results for the First Quarter of 2026

evidence.claim: Fluence Energy reported Q2 FY2026 backlog of about $5.6 billion as of March 31, 2026, a record level for the company, and reaffirmed FY2026 guidance.
evidence.source_title: Fluence Energy, Inc. Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results; Reaffirms Fiscal Year 2026 Guidance

evidence.claim: Freeport-McMoRan's 2025 annual report framed copper as core to its strategy and tied copper demand to secular trends in electrification and technological development.
Southern Copper's 1Q26 company presentation framed copper as a critical mineral for the energy transition, citing rising demand and potentially constrained supply growth.
evidence.source_title: Southern Copper Company Presentation - 1Q26 Production and Capex Guidance

evidence.claim: MP Materials announced a public-private partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense to accelerate an end-to-end U.S. rare earth magnet supply chain, with planned total U.S. rare earth magnet manufacturing capacity estimated at 10,000 metric tons after the new facility is completed.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Announces Transformational Public-Private Partnership with the Department of Defense

memory_update.text: Within the LNG/midstream part of the candidate chunk, WMB and ET have the clearest data-center/power-demand relationships because they disclose specific data-center or power-plant gas capacity projects and long-duration demand-pull contracts.
KMI is relevant to data-center power demand through gas-pipeline infrastructure but currently needs more customer/project-level evidence than WMB and ET before being upgraded in the Serenity funnel.

LNG is a global LNG export and gas-demand proxy, not a direct AI data-center power-delivery chokepoint; monitor whether U.S. domestic gas demand tightens feedgas costs or improves LNG contracting power.
FSLR has credible domestic solar manufacturing/backlog exposure, but the Serenity chokepoint remains downstream interconnection, transmission, storage, and firm capacity rather than modules alone.
FLNC maps to a plausible grid-flexibility chokepoint, but backlog-to-margin conversion and battery supply-chain risk are the decisive next validation points.

ENPH is lower priority for the AI/data-center power chokepoint because current evidence is dominated by residential solar cyclicality and U.S. policy headwinds; upgrade only if grid-edge/VPP or commercial storage evidence becomes material.
FCX and SCCO should be treated as broad copper commodity proxies for grid/electrification capex; Serenity validation requires copper market-pricing, supply-cost, and jurisdictional risk checks.
MP is strategically relevant to domestic rare earth magnets but is less direct to the immediate grid/data-center power chokepoint than natural-gas delivery, transformers, switchgear, and storage.

Need comparable valuation/crowding check across WMB, ET, KMI, LNG, FSLR, ENPH, FLNC, FCX, SCCO, and MP before any Layer 3 prioritization; this layer maps relationships only and does not make buy/sell recommendations.

Need standardized company-level metrics: percentage of EBITDA/revenue tied to target node, backlog/book-to-bill, contract duration, capex remaining, in-service schedule, regulatory risk, and margin sensitivity.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the candidate chunk spanning LNG export infrastructure, natural-gas midstream, solar, distributed/grid storage, copper, and rare earths. Serenity relevance is strongest inside this chunk for natural-gas pipeline names with explicit data-center or gas-fired power contracts/projects (WMB, ET, KMI), followed by grid-scale storage (FLNC) and domestic solar manufacturing (FSLR). Cheniere is more exposed to global LNG demand than the near-term U.S. data-center power chokepoint. Copper names remain broad commodity proxies for grid/electrification capex and need pricing/supply-cost checks. MP is a strategic U.S. magnet/rare-earth supply-chain name but less directly tied to immediate AI power delivery than gas, grid, transformer, and storage nodes.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify latest contracted capacity, expansion timing at Corpus Christi/Sabine Pass, feedgas sensitivity, spot-vs-contracted margin exposure, and whether data-center-driven U.S. gas demand affects feedgas costs more than LNG export margins.
ticker_relationships.node: LNG exports and global gas supply
ticker_relationships.relationship: Cheniere maps to LNG liquefaction/export capacity and long-term global gas demand rather than direct U.S. data-center power delivery. It can benefit if U.S. gas supply reliability and LNG contract demand remain scarce, but its Serenity chokepoint link is more global and contract-cycle dependent than grid-equipment or behind-the-meter power names.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track contract counterparties, firm-transportation rate economics, project in-service dates, permitting risk, capex-to-EBITDA conversion, and whether new gas demand is incremental or displaces other volumes.
ticker_relationships.node: Natural-gas transportation, storage, and data-center/power-plant laterals
ticker_relationships.relationship: Energy Transfer has a direct relationship to gas-fired power and data-center load through natural-gas pipeline capacity, storage, and announced projects serving power plants and data-center sites. The relationship is stronger than generic midstream because recent disclosures reference contracted demand-pull capacity and specific data-center/power customers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate NEO and Atlas economics, customer credit quality, regulatory approvals, turbine/generator procurement, gas supply availability, and whether behind-the-meter offerings create higher-return infrastructure revenue or only incremental pipeline throughput.
ticker_relationships.node: Natural-gas transmission, data-center behind-the-meter power, and pipeline constraints
ticker_relationships.relationship: Williams maps directly to gas infrastructure for AI/data-center power demand through Transco-linked expansions, behind-the-meter generation concepts, and specific data-center capacity agreements. Within this chunk, WMB has one of the clearest company-level links to the data-center power chokepoint.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check Creekside and other lateral projects, data-center/customer contracts, regional overlap with ERCOT/Southeast/PJM large-load growth, tariff terms, and new capacity vs. existing capacity utilization.
ticker_relationships.node: Natural-gas pipeline network and power-generation demand
ticker_relationships.relationship: Kinder Morgan maps to gas transport for LNG feedgas, industrial demand, and gas-fired power needs, with management materials positioning the network for surging data-center power demand. Relationship is credible but requires specific regional project/customer validation to separate chokepoint exposure from broad gas-pipeline beta.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track new bookings velocity, ASPs for 2029+ deliveries, utilization at U.S. vs. international plants, Section 45X/FEOC/Section 232 outcomes, cancellation clauses, and backlog margin conversion.
ticker_relationships.relationship: First Solar maps to domestic renewable generation supply and U.S. manufacturing scarcity, with a large contracted backlog and policy/tariff-linked domestic-content angle. Serenity relevance is moderate because solar generation still depends on interconnection, transmission, storage, and firming; its bottleneck is more domestic module availability and policy durability than immediate dispatchable power.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify channel inventory normalization, battery attach rates, VPP/utility program revenue, commercial product traction, U.S. vs. Europe recovery, tariff/45X effects, and whether grid-edge software becomes material to revenue.
ticker_relationships.node: Residential solar microinverters, batteries, and grid-edge energy management
ticker_relationships.relationship: Enphase maps to distributed energy and residential grid-edge flexibility rather than utility-scale AI power delivery. Current evidence shows weak U.S. residential demand after tax-credit expiration, so the Serenity relationship should remain lower priority unless batteries, virtual power plants, or commercial/grid-edge products show durable demand independent of residential solar cyclicality.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track backlog conversion to revenue/gross margin, order intake, domestic content/IRA exposure, battery-cell supply, customer concentration, grid-forming controls adoption, warranty provisions, and cash-flow quality.
ticker_relationships.node: Grid-scale battery storage, grid flexibility, and renewables integration
ticker_relationships.relationship: Fluence maps to grid-scale storage systems and software, a potential flexibility chokepoint as data-center load and renewables strain transmission and capacity markets. The relationship is meaningful, but backlog profitability, component sourcing, competition, and interconnection timing remain key validation items.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check current copper supply-demand balance, treatment/refining charges, Grasberg/Indonesia risk, U.S. copper policy, unit cash costs, production growth, and sensitivity to copper price vs. gold/moly byproducts.
ticker_relationships.node: Copper supply for grid expansion, electrification, data centers, and industrial infrastructure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Freeport-McMoRan maps to copper as an upstream material pulled by grid buildout, electrical equipment, data centers, and electrification. Serenity relevance is real but indirect: copper is a broad commodity exposure, so thesis quality depends on copper price, mine supply, jurisdictional risk, and cost curve rather than only AI power demand.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate 2026 production/capex guidance, project pipeline in Peru/Mexico, permitting/community risk, unit costs, dividend policy, reserve life, and realized copper price leverage.
ticker_relationships.node: Copper supply for energy transition and grid materials
ticker_relationships.relationship: Southern Copper maps to copper demand from energy transition, grid investment, and electrification. The relationship is broad and commodity-linked; Serenity relevance depends on whether SCCO offers differentiated production growth, cost advantage, or scarcity exposure relative to other copper producers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track magnetics ramp, DoD contract terms, heavy rare earth sourcing, NdPr pricing, customer/offtake volumes, China dependency reduction, separation yields, and whether energy-transition end markets become material revenue drivers.
ticker_relationships.node: Rare earth mining, separation, and U.S. magnet supply chain
ticker_relationships.relationship: MP Materials maps to critical minerals and magnet supply chains used in motors, defense, robotics, wind, and electrification. It is strategically relevant to energy and industrial electrification but less direct to the immediate AI data-center power bottleneck than gas pipelines, transformers, switchgear, and grid-scale storage.
